strings.name: 14th Dalai Lama
strings.summary: Recognized as the 14th Dalai Lama in childhood, Tenzin Gyatso received monastic training and went into exile in India in 1959. His nonviolent advocacy on Tibet and work on interfaith dialogue and public ethics earned the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize. He transferred political authority in 2011 while continuing religious activities. His succession policy conflicts with China’s position; his office apologized in 2023 after a video involving a boy caused controversy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: As a Tibetan Buddhist leader, he has long advocated nonviolence, religious dialogue and public ethics, and received the Nobel Peace Prize.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Taktser, Qinghai, in the traditional Tibetan region of Amdo.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Peace prize for nonviolence
strings.highlights.h1.text: Received the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize for nonviolent efforts toward a resolution of the Tibet question.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Monastic education; Geshe Lharampa degree in 1959.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Religion and public ethics
strings.highlights.h2.text: Promotes compassion, religious harmony and nonviolence; transferred political authority to elected leaders in 2011.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Confirms continuation
strings.timeline.t1.text: Said the Dalai Lama institution would continue, with his trust identifying the reincarnation; China takes a different position.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Apology over video with boy
strings.timeline.t2.text: His office apologized after criticism of a video involving kissing a boy and a request concerning his tongue.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Transfers political authority
strings.timeline.t3.text: Handed political authority to elected leaders while retaining his religious identity and activities.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Receives Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: The prize recognized his nonviolent advocacy.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Exile in India
strings.timeline.t5.text: Left Tibet after the Lhasa uprising and its suppression, later living in India.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Completes Buddhist examinations
strings.timeline.t6.text: Passed examinations at Lhasa’s Jokhang Temple and received the Geshe Lharampa degree.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Assumes political duties
strings.timeline.t7.text: Assumed political power as Chinese troops entered Tibet.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born into a farming family
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born Lhamo Dhondup to a Tibetan farming family in Taktser.
